title: Buffer Overflow in C++
description: An unbounded strcpy into a fixed-size buffer lets longer input overwrite adjacent memory.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.description: strcpy writes into a 64-byte buffer without checking the input length.
finding.why_dangerous: Writing past the buffer can corrupt memory and redirect control flow.
finding.impact: Memory corruption, remote code execution, crash (denial of service).
finding.fix: Use std::string or bounded operations like strncpy_s and check lengths.
learning_example: Input longer than what fits overwrites the stack beyond the buffer
std::string handles its own bounds so this overflow cannot happen

checklist: Never copy into fixed buffers without a length check
Prefer std::string / containers with automatic bounds
Use safe functions with explicit sizes when C APIs are required
Enable compiler defenses (ASLR, stack canaries, DEP)
Treat input length as data the program must validate
